function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)** | Topic | Summary | Practical Tips | |-------|---------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways, 35 mph on city streets.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | • Always obey posted signs; speed cameras and radar are common. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• Texas has a “no‑seat‑belt” law that imposes a fine of $200 for the driver and $100 for the passenger if no seat belt is used. | • Check that all occupants are buckled before starting the vehicle. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use is illegal while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is prohibited. | • Use a Bluetooth headset or voice‑activated controls. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02 % BAC).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, possible jail time. | • Designate a sober driver or use rideshare services if you’ve been drinking. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• Yield to emergency vehicles with lights and sirens. | • Always check both directions before turning or crossing. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during any weather that reduces visibility.
• Fog lights are only for foggy conditions. | • Keep headlights clean and properly aimed. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Towing requires a valid registration and insurance.
• Vehicles must display a valid license plate and registration sticker. | • Keep registration documents in the glove compartment. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, on sidewalks, or in designated no‑parking zones.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | • Always read parking signs and look for curb markings. | | **School Bus Rules** | • When a school bus stops and its red lights flash, all traffic must stop.
• In Texas, the bus must be stopped for at least 30 seconds after the lights stop flashing. | • Do not pass a stopped school bus until it resumes motion. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied or the vehicle is turning left. | • Signal early and check mirrors and blind spots. | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Texas uses speed cameras, red‑light cameras, and automated license‑plate readers. | • Drive defensively and stay within posted limits. | | **Penalties & Fines** | • Fines vary by offense but can range from $50 to $1,000+.
• Points are added to your driving record; 4 points can lead to license suspension. | • Keep a copy of any tickets and pay promptly to avoid additional penalties. | ### Quick Resources - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – [https://www.dps.texas.gov](https://www.dps.texas.gov) - **Texas Vehicle Code** – Available online for detailed statutes. Feel free to ask if you need more specific information (e.g., penalties for a particular offense, how to appeal a ticket, etc.).
